introduction.text: The Basilica di San Sebastiano fuori le mura is a minor basilica in Rome, built outside the Aurelian Walls, and historically significant as one of Rome’s Seven Pilgrim Churches and a site linked to early Christian martyrdom and pilgrimage traditions.

history.description: According to tradition, the catacombs beneath the basilica were used in 258 during the Valerian persecutions to bury Saints Peter and Paul.
The first basilica, the Basilica Apostolorum, was built by Constantine I in the first half of the 4th century.
St. Sebastian’s remains were moved to the basilica around 350.
The basilica was dedicated to Saint Sebastian in the 9th century.
In 826 the remains of St. Sebastian were transferred to St. Peter’s Basilica to protect them from a Saracen assault, after which the basilica was destroyed.
The basilica was refounded under Pope Nicholas I (858–867).
In the 13th century the arcade of the triple nave was walled in.
The martyr’s altar was reconsecrated by Pope Honorius III (1216–1227) at the request of the Cistercians.
After 1553, St. Philip Neri initiated the Seven Churches Visitation, making the basilica part of a one‑day pilgrimage.
The current edifice was largely rebuilt in the 17th century, commissioned by Cardinal Scipione Borghese in 1609 and completed by Giovanni Vasanzio after Ponzio’s death in 1613.
The Albani Chapel was built in 1716, designed by Carlo Maratta, Alessandro Specchi, Filippo Barigioni and Carlo Fontana, and commissioned by Pope Clement XI.
In 2001 the Bust of the Saviour by Gian Lorenzo Bernini was rediscovered in the convent adjacent to the church.

design.description: The basilica’s current layout was designed in the 17th century by Flaminio Ponzio and later completed by Giovanni Vasanzio.
The Albani Chapel, added in 1716, showcases Baroque design by Carlo Maratta, Alessandro Specchi, Filippo Barigioni and Carlo Fontana.
The nave’s triple arcade was walled in during the 13th century, altering the interior spatial arrangement.

art.description: A statue of St. Sebastian by Giuseppe Giorgetti stands at the altar in the first chapel on the left.
The Bust of the Saviour (Salvator Mundi) by Gian Lorenzo Bernini, rediscovered in 2001, is displayed in a niche on the right side.
The Chapel of Relics houses a stone allegedly imprinted with the footprints of Jesus and one of the arrows that struck St. Sebastian.
Busts of Saints Peter and Paul by Nicolò Cordier flank the altar, recalling the basilica’s original dedication.
